rv.q: Susan Stroman’s production and choreography are incandescent with energy and invention, and the company deliver performances of gut-punching power.
Audacious and troubling, it is delivered with brilliant precision here.
This West End transfer of Kander and Ebb's audacious musical set in Thirties Alabama is richly deserved.
This is a genuinely radical musical, full of stinging indignation and plaintive power...
'The Scottsboro Boys' is not an easy watch, but then neither should it be
So, yes, do rush to see this ingenious, pain-filled, feel-good show but be prepared to be ambushed by ambivalence.
It's easy to see The Scottsboro Boys soon inhabiting the same territory with its brilliant blend of incendiary rage, black humour and infectious tunes.
This is a short, punchy, superbly performed and fascinating evening that will shock you, educate you and entertain you.
A stunning cast of triple-threats are impressive from the off; and the direction and choreography of Susan Stroman is beautiful.

With its accomplished choreography, thought-provoking story and combination of raucous humour and heartbreaking truth and injustice, The Scottsboro Boys remains nonetheless a hard sell in today’s West End.

cn.t: Critics praise this daring Kander and Ebb musical for its provocative use of the minstrel show format to tell a harrowing true story, with Susan Stroman's incandescent direction and choreography earning particular acclaim alongside the stellar cast.
